setup.data: Synthetic hidden-Markov worlds where the Bayesian belief state is known exactly: hidden state = (task variable c, nuisance variable f); a reward at a query token reads only the class c, defining a closed-form reward-null kernel N_R split into a next-token-visible and a next-token-invisible component. Worlds: separable (main world xF=0.15, alphaF=0.95; second point; slow nuisance), visible-kernel control, entangled (filtering c needs f), Mess3. Action designs: tied (every token is an action, reference prefers among tied tokens), one-per-class, fresh tokens (uniform reference, built-in control). For LMs: in-context token streams from six HMMs (protocol and code of Balcells et al. 2026), 20,000-token streams; controlled GRPO on a six-letter stream with a query marker (2,048-token contexts, about 170 decisions per prompt).
setup.models: Toy: 4-layer pre-norm transformers (width 128, 4 heads, RMSNorm, rotary) and 2-layer GRUs (width 128), pretrained to within 5e-4 nat of Bayes-optimal loss; three pretraining seeds (plus 8 post-training seeds per pretrained model in the seed study). Post-training: SFT (demonstrator labels or Bayes action), DPO, GRPO (group 8), Dr. GRPO, REINFORCE, KL-RL with exact gradient, over beta including 0; 5,000 steps (50,000 in stress tests). LMs: base/post-trained checkpoint pairs Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-4B; controlled GRPO with LoRA rank 32 on Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base (also full fine-tuning of blocks 20-27).
setup.positions_layers: Query (decision) position vs ordinary positions; toy models measured at the query position at every depth for R; whole residual stream at all positions up to t' and all depths patched for filter-use test; LM probes on the residual stream of every layer, reported by relative depth (Figure 16).
setup.baselines: Base model (all quantities are post/base ratios); untrained network and last-eight-tokens baselines for decodability; exact Bayes filter for filter use; theoretical anchored optimum pi_beta* for policy sensitivity; random subspaces of the same dimension for interchange transfer.
setup.controls: Matched reward (SFT vs KL-RL beta=1, rewards 0.693 vs 0.691); matched KL (0.381); gauge control (scale kernel image by 0.1 and compensate at readout); random invertible map check on probe R2; frozen-at-base probe vs refit probe; head-only training; exact expected gradient (removes sampling noise); untied head; SGD vs AdamW; LoRA ranks; added next-token loss; weight decay stress test; uniform-reference fresh-token design; pre-registered subspaces, fate criteria and predictions.

key_results.claim: In exact worlds, post-training mostly reroutes or rescales reward-null information; it stays decodable.
key_results.quote: In controlled worlds, post-training mostly reroutes or rescales reward-null information and leaves it decodable.

key_results.claim: Erasure is rare and needs pressure outside the objective (prolonged weight decay) on distinctions nothing needs.
key_results.quote: Erasure appears only under prolonged weight decay, for distinctions that neither reward nor next-token prediction can see.

key_results.claim: SFT reroutes: the next-token-visible component stays decodable while the decision stops using it.
key_results.quote: After SFT the next-token-visible component is as decodable as before (Rvis = 0.98) and the decision has stopped responding to it (U = 0.15)

key_results.claim: At matched reward, KL-RL keeps use while SFT reroutes, so reward alone does not decide the fate.
key_results.quote: KL-RL at β = 1 and SFT reach the same reward, the first with (Rinv , U, A) = (1.00, 1.00, 0.69) and the second with (0.75, 0.15, 0.13).

key_results.claim: Use switches at a sharp anchor threshold while representation and allocation change smoothly.
key_results.quote: At the policy level the fate switches at a threshold in β, within (0.003, 0.02] for GRPO, whereas Rinv and A vary smoothly through it.

key_results.claim: Under weight-decay stress, the anchored policy keeps the visible component and most of the invisible one.
key_results.quote: Under the same pressure the anchored policy keeps the next-token-visible component intact, still reproduces the reference's log-odds (γ = 0.99), and retains 0.64 of the invisible component.

key_results.claim: In a GRU, rerouting can happen inside the computation: the filter stops using a component that is still half decodable.
key_results.quote: After SFT its filter all but stops using the invisible component (0.01 of the base) although half of it is still decodable from the same state

key_results.claim: Variance share falling is not information loss: most low-share runs keep R>=0.9.
key_results.quote: of the 172 runs whose kernel share fell below a tenth of the base, 153 keep R ≥ 0.9

key_results.claim: Low allocation makes information practically inaccessible to a new reader even when linearly decodable.
key_results.quote: Once that variance has dropped two-hundredfold, a network that still encodes the nuisance belief linearly (R2 = 0.93) is indistinguishable from an untrained one.

key_results.claim: In released Qwen3 checkpoints, decodability barely changes while late-layer effective rank drops.
key_results.quote: Post-training leaves both decodable: peak R2 changes by at most 0.05 for the belief state

key_results.claim: Late-layer spectral compression in the LMs is 12-19%.
key_results.quote: the effective rank of the later half of the network falls by 12 to 19%

key_results.claim: In Qwen3, unanchored coarse-class GRPO amplifies within-class log-odds instead of collapsing them.
key_results.quote: Without it they are amplified ten to twenty times and no run collapses

key_results.claim: Anchored training re-encodes what it keeps: the kernel subspace rotates by tens of degrees.
key_results.quote: At β = 0.04 the kernel's image in the residual stream rotates by 20 to 77 degrees.

key_results.claim: Frozen probes/subspaces misread re-encoding as erasure; refit on the model under test.
key_results.quote: A frozen diagnostic would read re-encoding as erasure, which is why every coordinate here is refit on the model under test.

key_results.claim: Two exits of one network: the policy exit stops using the kernel after SFT while the next-token exit keeps using it.
key_results.quote: After SFT the policy responds to a twin exchange at 0.15 of the base and the next-token head at 0.56.

key_results.claim: Ridge (penalized) probes read a change of allocation as loss of information.
key_results.quote: when the kernel component of an exactly embedded belief cloud is scaled by 0.03 and the readout compensated, the least-squares R2 of the kernel stays at 0.954 and the ridge R2 falls to 0.139.

methods.name: R/U/A three-coordinate fate test (represented, used, allocated)
methods.what_it_measures: For a subspace S: R = refit linear recoverability (whitened least squares, folds split by sequence), U = causal sensitivity of the decision to S via twin exchange, A = share of activation variance carried by S; all as post/base ratios.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 6 erased (R falls), 2 bypass / 3 not routed (R stays, U falls = their 'rerouted'), and separates both from harmless rescaling (A falls only).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Interchange intervention on the subspace image; gauge control; revival test.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: A candidate correctness subspace, matched item pairs, a reference condition (no pressure) to take ratios against; cheap (forward passes and linear fits) at 9B-27B.
methods.code_available: Not given in the paper text (pre-registration 'committed to the repository' but no URL); LM experiments reuse the released code of Balcells et al. (2026).

methods.name: Twin exchange (probe-free use measurement)
methods.what_it_measures: Response of the decision to swapping inputs that agree on the reward-relevant variable and differ only along the kernel (mean norm of the difference of centered log-policies).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 2 bypass vs 4 override: if the action no longer responds to the correctness-relevant difference, use is gone without needing a probe.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Restrict the swap to a subspace (interchange) and report the transferred fraction vs random subspaces of the same dimension.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Pairs of prompts matched on pressure and surface, differing only in the correctness-relevant content (e.g. same pushback, different true answer or different prior confidence). 16,384 pairs in toy; 128 twin pairs / 43,582 decisions in Qwen3.

methods.name: Frozen-at-reference probe vs refit probe, plus subspace rotation angle
methods.what_it_measures: Whether the same information is still there but re-encoded: frozen probe/subspace fails while refit probe and refit subspace work; rotation of the subspace image measured in degrees.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 5 transformed vs 6 erased; also tests H3 (probes trained on normal behaviour miss transformed failures).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Interchange on base-fitted vs refit subspace (0.78-0.88 vs 0.94-0.97 transfer in their anchored runs).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Activations under no-pressure and pressure conditions at the same layers; linear fits; principal angles between fitted subspaces.

methods.name: Two-exit test
methods.what_it_measures: Use of the same subspace by two readouts of one network (policy head at the decision vs next-token head).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 2 bypass / 3 not routed at the decision only: information is used by one output path and not by the one that acts.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Locate where the paths split; patch the subspace into the failing path.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Two readouts of the same forward pass (e.g. the answer token after pushback vs a verification/restatement token); cheap.

methods.name: Within-class slope and intercept regression (gamma, shift)
methods.what_it_measures: Least-squares fit of the policy's log-odds on the reference's log-odds across items: slope = item-wise use of the reference's distinctions, intercept = history-independent shift.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 4 override (slope kept, large global shift) vs 2 bypass/collapse (slope near 0) vs 1 readout/threshold (slope kept, offset only near the boundary).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Check which training objective or prompt component produces the shift; KL anchor restores slope 1.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Per-item log-odds (correct vs pushed answer) with and without pressure; trivial compute.

methods.name: Gauge control (rescale subspace image and compensate at readout)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a metric is an information/use measure (invariant) or an allocation measure (changes).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Guards against reading rescaling as erasure (6) or as a threshold failure (1).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Validates probes and interchange metrics before using them on real models.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: One trained model; apply an invertible linear map at a layer and its inverse downstream.

methods.name: Revival test (new linear readout on a frozen network; steps to 95%)
methods.what_it_measures: How accessible a still-decodable distinction is to a new reader under a fixed adaptation budget.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: The 'inaccessible' variant of 3 not routed: decodable with enough data but too low-variance to be picked up cheaply.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Relate accessibility to variance share; test whether a fix raises share.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Frozen activations plus a small head trained with SGD/AdamW; cheap.

methods.name: Whole-state filter-use patching
methods.what_it_measures: Use of a component by the model's own state update: patch the residual stream at all positions up to t' and all depths with a twin's component, read KL of later next-token distributions relative to the exact Bayes filter.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 3 not routed inside the computation (component present but not used by later processing).
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Lag curves Ufilt(k) over read-out offsets.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Twin pairs and full-state patching; more expensive (all layers and positions).

methods.name: Second-moment decomposition of the decision representation
methods.what_it_measures: Shares of the second moment carried by the mean, class features, nuisance features and their interaction over training.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Global shift (mean/collective mode) vs item-wise change; relates to 4 override by a constant push.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Predicts collapse vs amplification via the rate ratio.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Activations at the decision position grouped by class and nuisance labels.

controls_worth_copying: Report every quantity as a ratio to a reference condition (base model there; no-pressure condition for us).
Refit probes and subspaces on the model/condition under test, and also report a frozen-at-reference probe; disagreement indicates re-encoding.
Use whitened, unpenalized least-squares probes; check R2 is unchanged under a random invertible map of the activations.
Interchange interventions against random subspaces of the same dimension.
Gauge control: rescale the candidate subspace and compensate downstream; metrics that move are allocation, not information.
Matched-outcome comparisons (matched reward, matched KL) to separate the fate from how far the model moved.
Baselines for decodability: untrained network and a last-few-tokens baseline.
Built-in negative control where the decision should never read the subspace (fresh tokens, uniform reference).
Exact-gradient and head-only controls to rule out sampling noise and locate whether a change is written in the shared representation.
Separate pretraining-seed from post-training-seed variance; pre-register subspaces, fate criteria and predictions before each batch.

pitfalls.pitfall: A probe or subspace frozen at the reference model reads re-encoding (rotation) as erasure.
pitfalls.quote: A frozen diagnostic would read re-encoding as erasure, which is why every coordinate here is refit on the model under test.

pitfalls.pitfall: Penalized (ridge) probes confuse lower variance with lost information.
pitfalls.quote: when the kernel component of an exactly embedded belief cloud is scaled by 0.03 and the readout compensated, the least-squares R2 of the kernel stays at 0.954 and the ridge R2 falls to 0.139.

pitfalls.pitfall: Effective rank, spectral decay and variance share are not invariants of information or use.
pitfalls.quote: Spectral compression alone cannot identify information loss.

pitfalls.pitfall: Patching one layer or one position can be undone downstream, so null patching results may be false negatives.
pitfalls.quote: Patching a single layer or position is undone by the layers and positions left untouched, which is why the whole state is used.

pitfalls.pitfall: In a transformer an exchanged component can be recomputed from the tokens left in place, making use ratios noisy.
pitfalls.quote: A transformer recomputes part of an exchanged component from the tokens left in place

pitfalls.pitfall: Within-sequence interleaved probe splits inflate decodability for slowly mixing processes (note: their own LM probe for the invisible component then uses ridge, which their own appendix warns reads allocation as loss).
pitfalls.quote: because interleaved splits within one sequence reward slowly mixing processes

pitfalls.pitfall: Linear probes count a distinction kept only in a nonlinear code as lost.
pitfalls.quote: Represented information is measured with linear probes, so a distinction that survives only in a nonlinear code is counted as lost.

pitfalls.pitfall: A difference between conditions can just reflect how far the model moved; compare at matched distance.
pitfalls.quote: The divergence at the policy level is not a consequence of unanchored runs travelling farther.

limitations_quote: The exact ground truth that makes the three fates identifiable exists only in small hidden Markov worlds, with a one-step decision whose action is not fed back into the context.
future_work_quote: Whether a multi-step task, in which the policy also changes which histories are visited, moves the quotient or only the support of the belief state remains to be studied.

bears_on_fates.how: Their 'rerouted' (R stays, U falls) is our bypass: SFT and unanchored policy gradient leave the information decodable (R_vis 0.96-0.98) while the decision stops reading it (U 0.15-0.22); the two-exit test shows one head using it and the other not.
Erasure needed 50k steps of weight decay and occurred only for distinctions no term of the objective needs; a claim of erasure should come with refit probes at all depths and positions.
Anchored training re-encodes kept information (subspace rotates 20-77 degrees); a frozen probe fails while a refit probe works. This is the operational test for transformed vs erased.
GRU filter stops using a component that is half decodable from the same state; revival test shows decodable-but-inaccessible information when variance share is tiny.

Unanchored runs produce a history-independent shift (intercept 4.6-6.1 nats) that dominates item-wise information while R_vis stays 0.96-0.97; the slope/intercept regression separates a global push from loss of item-wise use. Analogy only: no user pressure is studied.
Rescaling (A falls, R and U kept) shows variance can shrink without any failure; this is a warning not to mistake low variance for a threshold problem, not a test for it.

bears_on_group_angle: Strongly relevant as method and as warning. It works at the subspace level throughout (the whole reward-null kernel and its components, not a single direction), measures rotation of a subspace's image across conditions in degrees (a Grassmannian distance), and decomposes the decision representation's second moment into mean/class/nuisance/interaction groups. The warning: Proposition 1 shows an invertible linear map preserves all probe information and interchange effects while setting the covariance to almost anything, so variance-based group statistics (PCA share, effective rank, and, by extension, covariance-based RSA/CKA comparisons across pressures) can change without any change in information or use. Any group-geometry comparison of flipped vs resisted items, or across pressures for H1, should be paired with refit probes and interchange tests, and the Procrustes/principal-angle idea should be run as 'frozen vs refit' to separate transformed from erased.
architecture_location: Little component-level localization (no attention vs MLP analysis). Architecture class matters: a GRU must carry the state, so it loses freed information everywhere and keeps protected information everywhere, whereas a transformer can recompute the belief from context at the decision position, so the decision position can differ from ordinary positions. In Qwen3-1.7B/4B and Qwen3.5-4B checkpoint pairs, belief-state decodability is nearly unchanged at every relative depth while effective rank falls 12-19% in the later half; under controlled GRPO the collapsed or amplified log-odds are written in the residual stream (head-only training does not collapse), and fully fine-tuning only blocks 20-27 amplifies like LoRA on all blocks. Outcomes are consistent across post-training seeds but depend on the pretrained model; the anchor verdict repeats in two Qwen3 sizes (one family only).
actionable_fix: Training: keep a KL anchor (beta of a few hundredths or more) when post-training so the decision keeps using distinctions the reference used; unanchored RLVR (beta=0, common in current recipes) or SFT on fixed labels reroutes. For our Stage B: plain DPO behaves like anchored RL here, while SFT-style fixes are expected to hide (reroute) rather than remove; recheck with R (refit and frozen), U (twin exchange) and A separately. Monitoring: do not use effective rank or variance share as a sign of information loss; refit probes per condition; measure use with matched twin pairs. A next-token loss restores use in recurrent models but not in transformers.
reuse_verdict: adapt - copy the R/U/A decomposition, twin-exchange use measure, frozen-vs-refit probe, two-exit test, gauge control and slope/intercept regression into Stage A/B; do not carry over the findings, which come from toy HMM worlds and synthetic in-context streams at 1.7-4B, not factual tasks under pressure.
relevance_to_project: Methodologically one of the closest papers to our fate taxonomy: it makes erased / rerouted (bypass) / re-encoded (transformed) operationally distinct and supplies concrete controls for each. It is less relevant on substance than its title suggests: it studies what training does to information the reward ignores, not what happens at inference when user pressure flips an answer, and its LM evidence is synthetic HMM streams on Qwen3 1.7-4B. The most useful transfer is the measurement design, especially refit-vs-frozen probes and probe-free twin tests of use.
